title: openai-compat-v12-tool-handshake-and-jsonschema-preserve
author: Maya Singh
release_notes: OpenAI Responses v12 compatibility: preserve JSON Schema structured-output fields, forward deterministic seed hints and nested metadata, improve tool/function-call handshake for streaming, and harden chunk reassembly/backpressure. No user-facing breaking changes. Rollout as canary then global.
description:
Context: Customers are adopting the newer OpenAI Responses variants that include explicit JSON Schema structured output and richer seed/determinism hints. Previous adapters dropped nested attribute namespaces and occasionally dropped tool-call 'handshake' signals under high-concurrency streaming, resulting in incorrect structured outputs and flaky tool invocations. This PR introduces an upgraded compatibility bridge for Responses v12 (and v12beta) to preserve and forward: 1) JSON Schema/structured-output envelope fields, 2) seed/determinism hints and rng annotations, and 3) nested metadata provenance (trace, source, request-id) through both streaming and final non-stream paths.

Motivation: keep downstream consumers (tooling, evals, observability) deterministic and compatible when switching to new OpenAI-style Responses while maintaining production-grade streaming stability.

Summary of changes:
- Bridge: add explicit mapping rules for Responses v12 structured fields -> redwood \"attributes\" envelope; preserve user-provided JSON Schema keys verbatim and expose schema validation errors as structured diagnostics.
- Tool handshake: implement a lightweight two-phase \"handshake\" in the tool-call path so tool endpoints receive a deterministic invocation token and declared schema before tokenized stream begins; handshake survives transient reconnects and uses the request-level seed for deterministic tool behaviour.
- Streaming stability: improve chunk reassembly by adding sequence checks and idempotent merge logic (handles partial bytes and out-of-order chunks from proxy layers). Add adaptive backpressure that signals upstream when KV cache warmup increases per-token latency.
- Metadata passthrough: threaded nested metadata (source.trace_id / source.span / provenance) through the bridge and keep the original namespaced keys on the Redwood side for observability and auditing.
- Tests: add unit tests for schema passthrough and handshake, integration tests that exercise streaming reconnects and tool replays, and e2e with the Python SDK sample that exercises function-calling.
- Docs: new compatibility doc outlining behavior and recommended rollout (canary 5% -> 25% -> 100%), and changelog entries for the API surface.

Checklist:
- [x] adapter mappings implemented
- [x] handshake protocol added and documented
- [x] streaming reassembly/backpressure fixed and load-tested
- [x] unit/integration/e2e tests included
- [x] CI green and canary rollout plan added

Performance notes: under synthetic bench this change added ~0.3ms median per-request overhead for handshake on streaming function calls but reduced 99th percentile errors for tool calls by ~87% on the canary fleet. Related: ENG-1428 (Responses v12 compatibility), SUP-88 (customer-reported flaky toolcall under streaming).
